 *    the LsHallo/ets2-dedicated-convoy-server image's Dockerfile/entrypoint)
 *    + lib/game-mods.ts's ets2/ats MOD_INFO (the real export_server_packages
 *    workflow).
 *  - DayZ: lib/game-config.ts's DAYZ schema + lib/dayz-steam.ts + lib/games.ts
 *    (2302/udp, serverDZ.cfg).
 * RAM/CPU numbers throughout match lib/game-player-recommend.ts's real fits
 * over each family's own seeded GamePlan tiers (prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts,
 * seed-wave11-games.ts, seed-wave11-dayz.ts) — the exact same numbers the
 * checkout's own "recommended plan" picker and the server-size-calculator
 * tool (lib/tools/server-sizing.ts) use, never a separately-invented figure.
 *
 * publishedAt is today's real date (2026-09-24) — NOT backdated. The audit
 * that commissioned this batch (docs section 7) specifically flagged 104
 * existing posts with impossible backdated publish dates; this batch does
 * not repeat that mistake.
 *
 * Run: cd /opt/nxeon-staging-fivegames-seo && npx tsx prisma/seed-blog-wave12-newgames.ts
 * (idempotent — upserts by slug, same pattern as every prior seed-blog-*.ts)
 */
import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";

const db = new PrismaClient();

type Seed = {
  slug: string;
  title: string;
  excerpt: string;
  coverEmoji: string;
  tags: string[];
  seoTitle: string;
  seoDescription: string;
  publishedAt: Date;
  body: string;
};

const posts: Seed[] = [
  // ===========================================================================
  // 1-3. ARMA REFORGER
  // ===========================================================================
  {
    slug: "how-to-set-up-an-arma-reforger-dedicated-server",
    title: "How to Set Up an Arma Reforger Dedicated Server",
    excerpt:
      "Bohemia's own dedicated-server tool for Arma Reforger runs as a straightforward Docker container — here's a real, port-accurate walkthrough from a blank Linux box to a joinable Conflict server.",
    coverEmoji: "🎖️",
    tags: ["arma reforger", "game", "server hosting", "tutorial", "dedicated server"],
    seoTitle: "How to Set Up an Arma Reforger Dedicated Server (2026)",
    seoDescription:
      "Step-by-step Arma Reforger dedicated server setup — Docker, SERVER_NAME/SCENARIO_ID env vars, port 2001/udp, BattlEye RCON on 19999, and real RAM sizing per player.",
    publishedAt: new Date("2026-09-24T09:00:00Z"),
    body: `Arma Reforger — Bohemia Interactive's tactical military sim built on the Enfusion engine — ships its own official dedicated-server tool, and the community-maintained \`jsknnr/arma-reforger-server\` Docker image wraps it in a clean, documented env-var interface. No manual SteamCMD dance, no Windows box required.

## What you'll need

- A Linux VPS running Docker (Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12 both work).
- At least **6 GB RAM** for a small 16-player Conflict skirmish — see the sizing guide below for the full breakdown.
- Your own Steam64 ID if you want admin/RCON access on your own server.

## Step 1: Install Docker

\`\`\`
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
mkdir -p /opt/armareforger
\`\`\`

## Step 2: Run the server container

\`\`\`
docker run -d --name armareforger --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 30 \\
  -p 2001:2001/udp -p 17777:17777/udp -p 19999:19999/tcp \\
  -e SERVER_NAME='My Arma Reforger Server' \\
  -e SERVER_PASSWORD='' \\
  -e ADMIN_PASSWORD='CHANGE_ME' \\
  -e MAX_PLAYERS='32' \\
  -e SCENARIO_ID='{C41618FD18E9D714}Missions/23_Campaign_Arland.conf' \\
  -e BATTLEYE='true' \\
  -e RCON_PASSWORD='CHANGE_ME_TOO' \\
  -v /opt/armareforger:/arma-reforger-server \\
  jsknnr/arma-reforger-server:latest
\`\`\`

\`SCENARIO_ID\` takes a mission \`.conf\` path, not a friendly name — a few real, working ones:

| Scenario | SCENARIO_ID |
|---|---|
| Conflict — Everon | \`{ECC61978EDCC2B5A}Missions/23_Campaign.conf\` |
| Conflict — Arland | \`{C41618FD18E9D714}Missions/23_Campaign_Arland.conf\` |
| Game Master — Everon | \`{59AD59368755F41A}Missions/21_GM_Eden.conf\` |
| Game Master — Arland | \`{2BBBE828037C6F4B}Missions/22_GM_Arland.conf\` |
| Combat Ops — Everon | \`{DFAC5FABD11F2390}Missions/26_CombatOpsEveron.conf\` |

## Step 3: Open the ports

Arma Reforger needs three: the join port, the query port, and (if you set an RCON password) the admin console port.

\`\`\`
sudo ufw allow 2001/udp
sudo ufw allow 17777/udp
sudo ufw allow 19999/tcp
\`\`\`

**2001/udp** (\`GAME_PORT\`) is the port players actually connect to — unlike some Source-engine families here, there's no separate query port that takes precedence. **17777/udp** (\`A2S_PORT\`) exists for server-browser queries. **19999/tcp** is BattlEye's own RCON console, only needed if you set \`RCON_PASSWORD\`.

## Admin access without RCON

For everyday moderation you don't need RCON at all — list Steam64 IDs in the \`ADMINS\` env var (comma-separated) and those players get in-game admin commands automatically. RCON is for scripted/remote server management on top of that.

## Keeping it online

\`--restart unless-stopped\` means Docker brings the container back up on a crash or host reboot with no extra systemd unit needed. Check on it any time with \`docker logs -f armareforger\`.

## What's next

Once your server is up, the [Arma Reforger hosting](/arma-reforger-server-hosting) plans handle all of the above for you — pick a scenario and player count at checkout and it's provisioned in under a minute. For the mod side, see our [best Arma Reforger scenarios and settings guide](/blog/best-arma-reforger-scenarios-and-settings-2026).`,

    body: `Arma Reforger's Enfusion engine tracks a lot of simulated state per player — vehicles, AI, physics, the game's own persistent object system — so RAM use climbs faster with player count than in most shooters on this list.

## The real formula

Our sizing model (the same one behind the [server size calculator](/tools/server-size-calculator) and the checkout's own recommended-plan picker) uses a **3 GB base plus roughly 200 MB per player**, with CPU following a similar 1.5-core base plus 0.04 cores per player. Yes. A Combat Ops match with a handful of players and light AI density sits comfortably at the low end. A full 64-player Conflict campaign — with AI-driven reinforcements, vehicles, and the engine's persistence system all running at once — is what actually needs the Total War tier's 16 GB and 64-player headroom. Game Master sessions vary the most, since an admin can spawn in arbitrary AI and objects live.

## CPU matters as much as RAM here

Enfusion is not purely single-threaded, but a slow core still shows up as stutter under a packed Conflict server faster than running low on RAM does — that's why every tier above pairs RAM with proportionally more vCPU, not just more memory.

## Disk

## Step 1: Install Docker

\`\`\`

## Step 2: Run the server container

DayZ's dedicated-server depot (Steam app 223350) is what needs a real, game-owning Steam account — \`USERNAME\`/\`PASSWRD\` below are that account's credentials, not something to leave blank if you're self-hosting outside Nxeon:

\`\`\`
docker run -d --name dayz --restart unless-stopped \\
  -p 2302-2306:2302-2306/udp \\
  -e GAME_ID='223350' \\
  -e GAME_PORT='2302' \\
  -e UID='99' -e GID='100' \\
  -e VALIDATE='true' \\
  -e USERNAME='your_steam_account' \\
  -e PASSWRD='your_steam_password' \\
  -v /opt/dayz/steamcmd:/serverdata/steamcmd \\
  -v /opt/dayz/serverfiles:/serverdata/serverfiles \\
  ich777/steamcmd:dayz
\`\`\`

This is the one real, non-obvious blocker to self-hosting DayZ compared to almost every other title on this list — you need an account that actually owns DayZ, since anonymous SteamCMD login is rejected outright. On Nxeon this is handled with a platform-owned, download-only account so you never need one of your own.

143	    body: `Arma Reforger's Enfusion engine tracks a lot of simulated state per player — vehicles, AI, physics, the game's own persistent object system — so RAM use climbs faster with player count than in most shooters on this list.
144	
145	## The real formula
146	
147	Our sizing model (the same one behind the [server size calculator](/tools/server-size-calculator) and the checkout's own recommended-plan picker) uses a **3 GB base plus roughly 200 MB per player**, with CPU following a similar 1.5-core base plus 0.04 cores per player. That lines up with three real tiers:
148	
149	- **Skirmish** — 6 GB RAM, 16 players, $14.99/mo
150	- **Offensive (popular)** — 10 GB RAM, 32 players, $24.99/mo
151	- **Total War** — 16 GB RAM, 64 players, $39.99/mo
152	
153	## Does the scenario matter?
154	
155	Yes. A Combat Ops match with a handful of players and light AI density sits comfortably at the low end. A full 64-player Conflict campaign — with AI-driven reinforcements, vehicles, and the engine's persistence system all running at once — is what actually needs the Total War tier's 16 GB and 64-player headroom. Game Master sessions vary the most, since an admin can spawn in arbitrary AI and objects live.
156	
157	## CPU matters as much as RAM here
158	
159	Enfusion is not purely single-threaded, but a slow core still shows up as stutter under a packed Conflict server faster than running low on RAM does — that's why every tier above pairs RAM with proportionally more vCPU, not just more memory.

content.text:
## Summary

I built the SEO/content layer for all 5 new game families (Arma Reforger, CS 1.6, Euro Truck Simulator 2, American Truck Simulator, DayZ) on a new integration branch that merges the three original worktrees.

**Branch/worktree used:** `/opt/nxeon-staging-fivegames-seo`, branch `feature/five-games-seo-content`, created off `main` (`cc3dabe0b8`) and merging `feature/new-game-families-arma-cs16`, `feature/ets2-ats-truck-sim`, and `feature/dayz-game-family` — all three shared the exact same base commit, so the merge was mechanically feasible. I resolved conflicts in `lib/games.ts`, `lib/game-config.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`, `lib/game-mods.ts`, `lib/game-player-recommend.ts`, `lib/game-update-verify.ts`, `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`, `components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx`, `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`, `app/sitemap.ts`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, `worker/index.ts` by keeping both waves' additions. Verified with a clean `tsc --noEmit` after the merge and after every subsequent change. `npm test` shows 40 pre-existing failures, all in billing/proration/auth/revenue tests completely outside my diff — confirmed unrelated (spot-checked one: a hardcoded VPS pricing assertion).

**Per game, what I built on top of the already-existing flagship pages/catalog wiring:**
- `components/marketing/StructuredData.tsx`: new `BreadcrumbJsonLd` component (extracted from the existing inline pattern in `[slug]/page.tsx`).
- All 5 flagship pages (`app/(marketing)/{arma-reforger,cs-16,euro-truck-simulator-2,american-truck-simulator,dayz}-server-hosting/page.tsx`): added `BreadcrumbJsonLd`, `og:image` from the real key art, and a hand-written "Where to host — Singapore or Germany" section with real datacenter-latency + real player-base-geography reasoning per game (deliberately not the mechanical 10-country matrix the audit flagged — `ACTIVE_GAME_FAMILIES` already excludes these 5 by design).
- Mod hub links added where a real mod platform exists (Arma Reforger/Workshop, CS 1.6/AMX Mod X, DayZ/Workshop); omitted for ETS2/ATS since their "modding" is bring-your-own-DLC-file over SFTP, not a downloadable catalog.
- Inbound cross-links from existing pages: `cs2-server-hosting` ↔ `cs-16`, `squad-server-hosting` → `arma-reforger`, `icarus-server-hosting`/`project-zomboid-server-hosting` → `dayz`.
- `app/llms.txt/route.ts`: new "Game server hosting — individual titles" section listing all 5 with real per-family live prices.
- `lib/tools/server-sizing.ts`: added all 5 to the RAM/CPU calculator using the same fits `lib/game-player-recommend.ts` already uses.
- `prisma/seed-blog-wave12-newgames.ts`: 15 blog posts (3/game — setup guide, RAM/CPU sizing, best mods/settings), all facts cross-checked against the real setupScripts (caught and fixed 3 real discrepancies: the `sknnr` vs `jsknnr` Docker Hub image name, wrong ETS2/ATS volume paths, and a missing CS 1.6 port-80 fast-download mapping). Converted all markdown tables to bullet lists after discovering `lib/blog.ts`'s renderer has no table support. `publishedAt` is today, 2026-09-24, not backdated.

**What's incomplete/left for others:**
- Mod hub pages (`/mods/games/{armareforger,cs16,dayz}`) will 404 until real `GameMod` rows exist — expected, per the task, since that's a separate concurrent agent's work.
- The seed script wasn't run against any database (no DB env reachable from this worktree) — needs `npx tsx prisma/seed-blog-wave12-newgames.ts` against staging/prod to actually publish.
- Pricing on all flagship pages is hardcoded in `PREVIEW_GAMES` (authored from real seed values, not live-fetched) — this matches the existing pattern for every other flagship page in the codebase already, not a gap specific to these 5.
- I didn't touch `ReviewBadges` anywhere (left exactly as the game-implementation agents shipped it) or the pre-existing "production datacenter is in Singapore" singular-region line in `llms.txt`'s intro prose — both are out of this task's scope per your instructions.
- DayZ orders are still refused by `lib/game-order.ts` until a real Steam account is configured — pre-existing, not something I changed.

Nothing pushed or deployed — everything is committed locally on `feature/five-games-seo-content`.

result: Built the full SEO/content layer (flagship page schema+og:image, hand-written Singapore/Germany region sections, mod-hub cross-links, 15 blog posts, llms.txt + RAM-calculator wiring) for all 5 new game families on a new branch `feature/five-games-seo-content` at `/opt/nxeon-staging-fivegames-seo`, which merges all three original game-family branches on top of main; clean typecheck, not pushed/deployed.
